title: A Food Critic Loses Her Sense of Smell

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上免费直播部分精选采访，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Yesterday, we told the story of a rare but severe symptom of long COVID.
sentences.zh: 昨天，我们讲述了一个罕见但严重的长新冠症状的故事。

sentences.en: A far more common symptom is the long-term loss of smell.
sentences.zh: 而一种更为常见的症状是长期丧失嗅觉。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Times restaurant critic Tejal Rao, recounts the quest to try to get hers back.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事，《纽约时报》餐厅评论家泰贾尔·拉奥将讲述她试图找回嗅觉的历程。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, March 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月23日，星期二。

sentences.en: I was in the bathroom at my home in Los Angeles, and I was stepping into the shower, and I smelled something really unfamiliar.
sentences.zh: 当时我在洛杉矶家里的浴室准备洗澡，突然闻到了一种非常陌生的味道。

sentences.en: I thought maybe it was stagnant water or the plastic of the shower cap that I was wearing to cover my hair.
sentences.zh: 我以为可能是死水，或者是为了保护头发而戴的浴帽上的塑料味。

sentences.en: I thought maybe it was the stone tiles.
sentences.zh: 我还以为是石砖的味道。

sentences.en: Like, had someone else just cleaned the bathroom?
sentences.zh: 比如，是不是刚才有人刚打扫过浴室？

sentences.en: I couldn't figure it out.
sentences.zh: 我怎么也想不明白。

sentences.en: And then after a few minutes, I realized it was actually a blank.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，我意识到其实是一片空白。

sentences.en: There was no smell.
sentences.zh: 什么味道都没有。

sentences.en: I had just lost my sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚失去了嗅觉。

sentences.en: Just like that.
sentences.zh: 就这样，毫无预兆。

sentences.en: And I still went ahead and took a shower, but the whole time I was sort of thinking, how soon can I get a test for, you know, how soon can I get tested for COVID?
sentences.zh: 我还是去洗了澡，但整个过程中我一直在想，我什么时候能去做个新冠检测？

sentences.en: I had very mild symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 我的症状非常轻微。

sentences.en: It was just like a rough flu or cold.
sentences.zh: 就像得了重感冒或流感一样。

sentences.en: I was exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我精疲力竭。

sentences.en: And my parents kept checking in, kept calling to remind me to eat.
sentences.zh: 我父母不停地打电话来询问，提醒我吃饭。

sentences.en: But I've never experienced a loss of appetite like that before.
sentences.zh: 但我以前从未经历过那样的食欲不振。

sentences.en: Any kind of meat made me feel a little bit queasy.
sentences.zh: 任何肉类都会让我感到有点恶心。

sentences.en: So like roast chicken, which is a real comfort food for me normally, was just very, very squishy.
sentences.zh: 比如烤鸡，这通常是我真正的慰藉食物，但当时吃起来感觉非常非常软烂。

sentences.en: And popcorn was like foam, but with sharp bits in it, like so unpleasant all of a sudden.
sentences.zh: 爆米花吃起来像泡沫，但里面又带着尖锐的碎屑，突然间变得非常令人不适。

sentences.en: Everything about it that's a joy was very unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 它原本所有令人愉悦的特质都变得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: I started to feel better in early to mid-January.
sentences.zh: 我在一月中旬左右开始感觉好转。

sentences.en: I didn't have to pass out and sleep for half the day.
sentences.zh: 我不再需要昏睡大半天了。

sentences.en: I could get back to work, but I still couldn't really smell anything.
sentences.zh: 我可以恢复工作，但我仍然什么都闻不到。

sentences.en: Smell is just, it's so crucial to taste, which means it's really crucial to everything that I do.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉对味觉至关重要，这意味着它对我所做的一切都至关重要。

sentences.en: I work as a restaurant critic, but I also develop recipes.
sentences.zh: 我是一名餐厅评论家，同时也负责研发食谱。

sentences.en: And it's really difficult to cook without a sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 没有嗅觉真的很难烹饪。

sentences.en: If you're not used to it, you don't know what's going on.
sentences.zh: 如果你不习惯，你就不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: It's almost like wearing a blindfold.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像蒙着眼睛一样。

sentences.en: If you lost your taste buds, I'm going to show you guys how to get it back real quick.
sentences.zh: 如果你失去了味蕾，我会教你们如何快速找回它。

sentences.en: I started looking up what people were doing to get back their sense of smell or, you know, different kinds of aromatherapies.
sentences.zh: 我开始查找人们为了找回嗅觉在做什么，或者尝试各种芳香疗法。

sentences.en: And I came across this TikTok video that had gone viral for a home remedy.
sentences.zh: 我偶然发现了一个在 TikTok 上疯传的家庭偏方视频。

sentences.en: You want to take a nice fresh orange and burn it all the way around.
sentences.zh: 你需要拿一个新鲜的橙子，把它彻底烧焦。

sentences.en: Make sure it's dark, charcoal, black.
sentences.zh: 确保它变得漆黑，像木炭一样。

sentences.en: This guy, Kamar Lalor, uploaded it.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫卡马尔·拉洛尔，他上传了这个视频。

sentences.en: After that, just cut it.
sentences.zh: 之后，把它切开。

sentences.en: Slice it down the middle.
sentences.zh: 从中间切开。

sentences.en: Burn an orange.
sentences.zh: 烧一个橙子。

sentences.en: A whole orange with the peel still on.
sentences.zh: 带皮的整个橙子。

sentences.en: You burn it.
sentences.zh: 把它烧焦。

sentences.en: You take the peel off.
sentences.zh: 把皮剥掉。

sentences.en: And then you mash the hot pulp of the orange with a little sugar and you eat it with a spoon.
sentences.zh: 然后把滚烫的橙肉捣碎，加一点糖，用勺子吃掉。

sentences.en: I'm no scientist, but it does work.
sentences.zh: 我不是科学家，但这确实有效。

sentences.en: I'm telling you, this is some Jamaican remedies.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你们，这可是牙买加的偏方。

sentences.en: It's going to work, I promise you.
sentences.zh: 它会起作用的，我向你们保证。

sentences.en: So I thought I would give it a try.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定试一试。

sentences.en: Okay, so I've got these tiny oranges.
sentences.zh: 好了，我拿到了这些小橙子。

sentences.en: They're so tiny, they're falling through the crate.
sentences.zh: 它们太小了，都从板条箱里掉出来了。

sentences.en: Charring an orange, according to Kimara's TikTok video, was sort of the big event at my house that day.
sentences.zh: 根据卡马尔的 TikTok 视频，烧焦橙子成了那天我家里的重大活动。

sentences.en: It was my partner, myself, our two dogs.
sentences.zh: 当时有我的伴侣、我，还有我们的两只狗。

sentences.en: We were all in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 我们都在厨房里。

sentences.en: There's a great way to spend the, um, what day is it?
sentences.zh: 这是度过……嗯，今天是星期几来着？

sentences.en: I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 是星期二。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不对。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 是星期三。

sentences.en: I think the dogs were probably wondering what we were doing.
sentences.zh: 我想狗狗们大概在纳闷我们在干什么。

sentences.en: They were getting very annoyed.
sentences.zh: 它们变得非常烦躁。

sentences.en: But, uh, we stood over the gas stove and charred some oranges.
sentences.zh: 但是，我们站在煤气灶前，烧焦了一些橙子。

sentences.en: The peel's coming off really easily.
sentences.zh: 皮剥起来很容易。

sentences.en: And tried to follow his instructions as closely as we could.
sentences.zh: 我们尽量严格按照他的说明去做。

sentences.en: I knew that it was a TikTok video.
sentences.zh: 我知道那只是个 TikTok 视频。

sentences.en: You know, it wasn't a scientific paper that I had read.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那不是我读过的科学论文。

sentences.en: But I was secretly really hopeful that it would work.
sentences.zh: 但我私下里真的非常希望它能奏效。

sentences.en: And, um, I can't smell it.
sentences.zh: 然后，嗯，我闻不到它。

sentences.en: And, um, and it was still, things were still really muted.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，一切仍然非常沉闷。

sentences.en: Still really flat.
sentences.zh: 依然非常平淡。

sentences.en: So I called up Kimar.
sentences.zh: 所以我给卡马尔打了电话。

sentences.en: That's the guy who made the TikTok.
sentences.zh: 就是那个制作 TikTok 视频的人。

sentences.en: To see if maybe I was doing it wrong.
sentences.zh: 想看看是不是我哪里做错了。

sentences.en: He was inside his car, parked outside his family restaurant where he works.
sentences.zh: 他当时坐在车里，停在他工作的家庭餐厅外面。

sentences.en: Now, um, we're located in Ontario, um, Toronto.
sentences.zh: 现在，嗯，我们在安大略省，嗯，多伦多。

sentences.en: They sell, like, goat curry and oxtail and roti.
sentences.zh: 他们卖咖喱山羊肉、牛尾和罗蒂饼之类的东西。

sentences.en: Jerk chicken, oxtail, curry goat, some nice rice, all that good stuff.
sentences.zh: 牙买加烤鸡、牛尾、咖喱山羊肉、美味的米饭，所有这些好东西。

sentences.en: Curry goat.
sentences.zh: 咖喱山羊肉。

sentences.en: Oh, that sounds so good.
sentences.zh: 哦，听起来太棒了。

sentences.en: And he was so optimistic.
sentences.zh: 他非常乐观。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, I told him that it didn't exactly work for me.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道，我告诉他这对我没起作用。

sentences.en: At least it didn't work the way it was advertised.
sentences.zh: 至少没有像宣传的那样起作用。

sentences.en: Like it would cure me in an hour.
sentences.zh: 比如它能在一小时内治好我。

sentences.en: I said, give it another try.
sentences.zh: 他说，再试一次。

sentences.en: Roast it again.
sentences.zh: 再烤一次。

sentences.en: Roast it for 12 minutes, though.
sentences.zh: 不过要烤12分钟。

sentences.en: He said that I should try it every day.
sentences.zh: 他说我应该每天都试一试。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: For 12 minutes.
sentences.zh: 烤12分钟。

sentences.en: And make sure to eat it hot.
sentences.zh: 一定要趁热吃。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And then he asked if I wanted to speak to his mom, who taught it to him.
sentences.zh: 然后他问我想不想和他妈妈说话，是她教给他的。

sentences.en: And I thought, yes, I'd love to speak to your mom.
sentences.zh: 我想，是的，我很想和你妈妈聊聊。

sentences.en: And he just, he's like, mom.
sentences.zh: 然后他直接喊道：妈。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi, Julian.
sentences.zh: 你好，朱利安。

sentences.en: And she came out and was equally, like, positive and joyful.
sentences.zh: 她走出来，同样表现得非常积极和快乐。

sentences.en: God bless.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: And, um, so thrilled that her family remedy had kind of traveled all around the world and people were trying it, even if it hadn't worked for everyone.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，她很高兴她的家庭偏方传遍了世界各地，人们都在尝试，即使它并没有对每个人都奏效。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Back home in Jamaica.
sentences.zh: 回到牙买加。

sentences.en: My mom gave us to his children then because she had 15 kids.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈那时把我们当孩子养，因为她有15个孩子。

sentences.en: And when we are sick and we don't have any taste and any kind of stuff there, she just roasts the orange and put the sugar on it and give us to eat.
sentences.zh: 当我们生病、失去味觉或者出现类似情况时，她就会烤个橙子，撒上糖，让我们吃掉。

sentences.en: And so we get back our taste and stuff and then we start to eat.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就能找回味觉之类的，接着就开始吃饭了。

sentences.en: Because that's what it's supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是它应该起的作用。

sentences.en: Get back your sense.
sentences.zh: 找回你的感官。

sentences.en: It's like it's sending something to your brain to reboost it.
sentences.zh: 就像是给你的大脑发送某种信号来重启它。

sentences.en: So the orange remedy didn't work as advertised for me.
sentences.zh: 所以，橙子偏方并没有像宣传的那样对我起作用。

sentences.en: But the thing that Trudianne said, that the brain needs some kind of reboost, that got me wondering, what is the connection between the brain and the nose?
sentences.zh: 但特鲁迪安说的话，即大脑需要某种重启，让我开始思考：大脑和鼻子之间到底有什么联系？

sentences.en: I did a little bit of research and I found a place called the Monell Chemical Census Center in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 我做了一些研究，发现费城有一个叫莫内尔化学感官中心的地方。

sentences.en: They do lots of different kinds of research on smell and on taste.
sentences.zh: 他们对嗅觉和味觉进行了各种各样的研究。

sentences.en: And I connected with a research scientist there, Dr. Pamela Dalton.
sentences.zh: 我联系了那里的研究科学家帕梅拉·道尔顿博士。

sentences.en: Well, I'm a basic research scientist who studies how people use their sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 我是一名基础研究科学家，研究人们如何使用嗅觉。

sentences.en: And she studies, among many, many other things, the ways that emotions can kind of change the way we smell things.
sentences.zh: 除了许多其他事情，她还研究情绪如何改变我们闻东西的方式。

sentences.en: Generally, when you lose your sense of smell under most circumstances,
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，当你失去嗅觉时，

sentences.en: it's because the molecules actually can't get into the olfactory receptor area of the nose because of congestion.
sentences.zh: 是因为分子由于充血实际上无法进入鼻子的嗅觉受体区域。

sentences.en: COVID is different in that way because most people who lost their sense of smell did so without having any nasal congestion whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 新冠在这方面有所不同，因为大多数失去嗅觉的人并没有任何鼻塞症状。

sentences.en: Pam explained that during the pandemic, you know, millions and millions of people lost their sense of smell just in an instant.
sentences.zh: 帕姆解释说，在疫情期间，你知道，数以百万计的人瞬间失去了嗅觉。

sentences.en: It was just like a light bulb got turned off or a switch got, you know, flicked off.
sentences.zh: 就像灯泡被关掉，或者开关被“啪”地关掉一样。

sentences.en: And one moment they could smell and the next moment nothing smelled.
sentences.zh: 前一刻他们还能闻到味道，下一刻就什么都闻不到了。

sentences.en: And even though that's how we lose our sense of smell, that's not how we get it back.
sentences.zh: 尽管这就是我们失去嗅觉的方式，但这并不是我们找回它的方式。

sentences.en: You know, there's not a switch that just kind of turns it back on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，并没有一个开关能直接把它重新打开。

sentences.en: We don't really understand how this system uses coding to develop all of the different smells that our brain is able to understand.
sentences.zh: 我们并不真正了解这个系统是如何利用编码来开发大脑能够理解的所有不同气味的。

sentences.en: So much of what we think of as taste is actually kind of happening in your nose and brain.
sentences.zh: 我们认为的味觉中，很大一部分实际上是在你的鼻子和大脑中发生的。

sentences.en: It's your smell receptors, your 400 smell receptors, and they're all working to identify millions and millions.
sentences.zh: 这是你的嗅觉受体，你有400个嗅觉受体，它们都在努力识别数以百万计的气味。

sentences.en: The estimate is a trillion smells.
sentences.zh: 据估计有万亿种气味。

sentences.en: That then is sort of a readout for the brain to say, oh, those five types of cells that are activated mean I'm smelling a flower versus, you know, a pizza or coffee in the morning.
sentences.zh: 然后大脑会读取这些信息，判断出：哦，那五种被激活的细胞意味着我闻到的是花，而不是早晨的披萨或咖啡。

sentences.en: But another thing she told me that made me feel a little optimistic is that olfactory receptor neurons are constantly regenerating every few weeks.
sentences.zh: 但她告诉我的另一件事让我感到有点乐观，那就是嗅觉受体神经元每隔几周就会不断再生。

sentences.en: Now, you, as an adult, have memories of what things should smell like.
sentences.zh: 现在，作为一个成年人，你对事物应该是什么味道有记忆。

sentences.en: And that's why we think the olfactory retraining may actually help.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们认为嗅觉训练可能真的有帮助。

sentences.en: Because you're connecting the central input, your representation of what your coffee should smell like, with the incoming molecular signals.
sentences.zh: 因为你正在将中央输入——你对咖啡应该是什么味道的认知——与传入的分子信号连接起来。

sentences.en: Smells are connected to memories and moods and feelings.
sentences.zh: 气味与记忆、情绪和感受是相连的。

sentences.en: One way of thinking about it is that there's this map in your brain that you can follow to get smells back.
sentences.zh: 一种思考方式是，你的大脑中有一张地图，你可以沿着它找回嗅觉。

sentences.en: But if your sense of smell has been gone for a long time, if you lose that map, it's more like starting from scratch.
sentences.zh: 但如果你的嗅觉已经消失了很长时间，如果你丢失了那张地图，那就更像是从零开始。

sentences.en: It's almost like if there's some, if there's some map intact, they can follow the right map to make the right connections.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，如果还有一些地图是完整的，它们就能沿着正确的地图建立正确的连接。

sentences.en: But if it's completely gone, they're just wiring, rewiring haphazardly.
sentences.zh: 但如果它完全消失了，它们就只是在胡乱地重新布线。

sentences.en: So I was really hopeful after talking with Pam that, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以在和帕姆交谈后，我真的很有希望，你知道，

sentences.en: maybe there would be some way to find my way back to smelling by doing this thing called olfactory training or smell training.
sentences.zh: 也许通过这种叫做嗅觉训练的方法，我能找到找回嗅觉的途径。

sentences.en: I just needed to learn how to actually do it.
sentences.zh: 我只是需要学习如何真正做到这一点。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用《纽约时报》一个月，而且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 这一个月你可以越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能读到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I think most people don't understand what smell training is.
sentences.zh: 我觉得大多数人并不了解什么是嗅觉训练。

sentences.en: And I could sum that up by saying it's not what your nose does, but rather what your brain does with the stimulation.
sentences.zh: 我可以总结一下，它不是关于你的鼻子做了什么，而是关于你的大脑如何处理这些刺激。

sentences.en: I called Chrissy Kelly, who founded Abscent in the UK, and that's Abscent as in smell.
sentences.zh: 我联系了在英国创立了Abscent的克丽丝·凯利（Chrissy Kelly），Abscent就是嗅觉（smell）的那个词。

sentences.en: I remember when I got 100 people in my Facebook group, which was called Smell Training, thinking, oh my God, wow, that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 我记得当我的Facebook群组“嗅觉训练”达到100人时，我心想，天哪，哇，太棒了。

sentences.en: And she started this online community.
sentences.zh: 她发起了这个在线社区。

sentences.en: And now we have 22.9 thousand.
sentences.zh: 现在我们已经有2.29万名成员了。

sentences.en: So there are a lot of us now.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有很多同伴。

sentences.en: And she lost her sense of smell back in 2012 after some kind of viral infection.
sentences.zh: 她在2012年因为某种病毒感染失去了嗅觉。

sentences.en: And at that time, doctors didn't really recommend anything.
sentences.zh: 当时，医生们并没有给出什么真正的建议。

sentences.en: But she read some research about smell training and how repetitive, structured sessions, smelling just four scents, could potentially help people start to orient themselves again,
sentences.zh: 但她读到了一些关于嗅觉训练的研究，了解到通过重复、结构化的训练，只闻四种气味，可能有助于人们开始重新定位自己，

sentences.en: pick up smells again.
sentences.zh: 重新拾回嗅觉。

sentences.en: I quickly got to the point where being a student of my affliction was better than being a victim of my affliction.
sentences.zh: 我很快就意识到，成为自己病症的研究者比成为病症的受害者要好。

sentences.en: And it became an absolute passion.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一种绝对的热情。

sentences.en: I wanted to formally learn what a smell training session should look like.
sentences.zh: 我想正式学习嗅觉训练课程应该是什么样子的。

sentences.en: And it's so much more like therapy than I expected it to be.
sentences.zh: 它比我预期的更像是一种治疗。

sentences.en: There is so much anxiety about getting it right in the beginning that I just think it's really valuable to say, OK, this is the program.
sentences.zh: 刚开始时，人们对于“做对”这件事有很大的焦虑，所以我认为明确告诉大家“这就是方案”非常有价值。

sentences.en: Start with this.
sentences.zh: 从这个开始。

sentences.en: So kind of like therapy, smell training works best if you're in a quiet space where you feel safe, where you can focus and think.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗅觉训练就像治疗一样，如果你在一个感到安全、安静的空间里，能够专注和思考，效果最好。

sentences.en: I sat down at my little desk in my office at home with a box of spices.
sentences.zh: 我坐在家里办公室的小桌前，拿着一盒香料。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And now for the first jar, I just want you to sit there with it with no expectations.
sentences.zh: 现在，对于第一个罐子，我只想让你坐在那里，不要有任何期待。

sentences.en: So she asked me to get four spices and not open them all immediately, open them one at a time.
sentences.zh: 她让我准备四种香料，不要立刻全部打开，要一次打开一个。

sentences.en: OK, so hold it up to your nose.
sentences.zh: 好的，把它举到鼻子前。

sentences.en: And I had cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, cumin.
sentences.zh: 我有小豆蔻、丁香、肉桂和孜然。

sentences.en: And I want you to just shut yourself down completely.
sentences.zh: 我希望你完全放空自己。

sentences.en: I think what she was saying is, you know, turn off the thoughts that are analyzing what's happening right now and just kind of be in the moment.
sentences.zh: 我想她表达的意思是，关掉那些正在分析当下情况的思绪，只是活在当下。

sentences.en: And just take little, I call them bunny sniffs, tiny little sniffs.
sentences.zh: 然后轻轻地吸气，我称之为“兔子嗅”，就是非常细微的吸气。

sentences.en: When I was smelling without her, when I was smelling on my own, I was taking these deep breaths and kind of trying to pull the aromas into my body.
sentences.zh: 当我没有在她的指导下自己闻的时候，我会深呼吸，试图把香气吸进身体里。

sentences.en: And that's actually, that doesn't work that well.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，那样做效果并不好。

sentences.en: So Chrissy suggested bunny sniffs, which is taking these teeny tiny little sniffs of air, you know, consecutive little sniffs.
sentences.zh: 所以克丽丝建议用“兔子嗅”，也就是连续进行非常细微的空气吸入。

sentences.en: Then you pause and then take a breath because we don't want you to faint and then go back to it again.
sentences.zh: 然后停顿一下，再呼吸，因为我们不想让你晕倒，然后再继续。

sentences.en: And I was immediately ready to say, I can't smell them very well.
sentences.zh: 我当时立刻就想说，我闻不太出来。

sentences.en: Well, it's kind of like the cloves were in the next room and I could hear them a little bit.
sentences.zh: 就像丁香在隔壁房间，我能隐约听到一点声音。

sentences.en: Like I could pick up a word every now and then, but I didn't know exactly what they were talking about.
sentences.zh: 就像我偶尔能捕捉到一个词，但不知道他们到底在说什么。

sentences.en: OK, so don't judge yet.
sentences.zh: 好的，先别急着下定论。

sentences.en: And before I could complain, Chrissy asked me to kind of slow down, take my time.
sentences.zh: 在我抱怨之前，克丽丝让我慢下来，慢慢来。

sentences.en: Don't say, oh, that was good or that wasn't good or I didn't get anything.
sentences.zh: 不要说，哦，这个好，那个不好，或者我什么都没闻到。

sentences.en: Just, just, just sit with it.
sentences.zh: 只是，只是，只是静静地感受它。

sentences.en: OK, the second one.
sentences.zh: 好的，第二个。

sentences.en: The second scent that we, that we smelled together was a jar of whole cardamom pods.
sentences.zh: 我们一起闻的第二种气味是一罐完整的豆蔻荚。

sentences.en: Cardamom is a really familiar smell to me.
sentences.zh: 豆蔻对我来说是一种非常熟悉的气味。

sentences.en: It's, it's part of the reason I picked it to be part of my smell kit.
sentences.zh: 这也是我把它选入嗅觉训练包的原因之一。

sentences.en: My mom uses it mostly paired with meat, like in lamb biryani.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈用它主要是搭配肉类，比如羊肉手抓饭。

sentences.en: There's often cardamom or in masala chai, in tea with boiled with spices and ginger.
sentences.zh: 通常会有豆蔻，或者在印度香料奶茶里，和香料、姜一起煮。

sentences.en: It's just a really familiar, delicate, floral scent.
sentences.zh: 那是一种非常熟悉、细腻、花香的气味。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Chrissy had me open the lid of the cardamom jar and she told me to close my eyes.
sentences.zh: 克丽丝让我打开豆蔻罐的盖子，并让我闭上眼睛。

sentences.en: I want you to imagine that you were looking into a really deep well.
sentences.zh: 我想让你想象你在注视着一口非常深的井。

sentences.en: So deep that you don't know when, you know, the coin you toss in is going to hit the bottom.
sentences.zh: 深到你不知道你扔进去的硬币什么时候会触底。

sentences.en: And to just keep listening.
sentences.zh: 只需要一直倾听。

sentences.en: So imagine that you are waiting and waiting and waiting.
sentences.zh: 所以想象你在等待，等待，再等待。

sentences.en: And people who have lost their sense of smell, I think that we smell more slowly.
sentences.zh: 我认为失去嗅觉的人，我们闻气味的速度更慢。

sentences.en: Chrissy used the term listening a lot when we were talking about smelling.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论嗅觉时，克丽丝经常使用“倾听”这个词。

sentences.en: It's like you're leaning in and you're trying to pick up as much as you can.
sentences.zh: 就像你在前倾，试图捕捉尽可能多的信息。

sentences.en: So smell is instantaneous for healthy people.
sentences.zh: 对于健康人来说，嗅觉是瞬间发生的。

sentences.en: And I think it takes a longer time for us to receive, for the receptors to work and to feed that into the brain.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们需要更长的时间来接收，让受体工作并将其传送到大脑。

sentences.en: You know, you throw the coin in and you wait.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你扔下硬币，然后等待。

sentences.en: And to kind of apply that to sniffing the cardamom pods.
sentences.zh: 把这个应用到闻豆蔻荚上。

sentences.en: And just keep listening.
sentences.zh: 一直倾听。

sentences.en: So let's give that one a go.
sentences.zh: 让我们试一试。

sentences.en: I'd forgotten that my grandfather, my mom's father, used to chew cardamom pods until I was doing this exercise.
sentences.zh: 在做这个练习之前，我已经忘了我祖父，也就是我妈妈的父亲，曾经有嚼豆蔻荚的习惯。

sentences.en: I think maybe to freshen his breath.
sentences.zh: 我想可能是为了清新口气。

sentences.en: I don't know why he did that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他为什么那么做。

sentences.en: But he was like my favorite grandparent.
sentences.zh: 但他是我最喜欢的祖辈。

sentences.en: We were very close.
sentences.zh: 我们非常亲近。

sentences.en: And he always smelled like cardamom.
sentences.zh: 他身上总是带着豆蔻的味道。

sentences.en: He died a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 他几年前去世了。

sentences.en: And when I was in the middle of this exercise, I remembered it.
sentences.zh: 当我在做这个练习时，我想起了这件事。

sentences.en: You know, and it opened up all these other memories that were connected to that.
sentences.zh: 它开启了所有与此相关的其他记忆。

sentences.en: All the tasks that we're doing right now, the concentrating, the thinking, the waiting, the anticipation,
sentences.zh: 我们现在做的所有任务，专注、思考、等待、期待，

sentences.en: all of those things are cognitive processes that happen higher up in the olfactory brain.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是发生在嗅觉大脑更高层面的认知过程。

sentences.en: I think of it more like a car that's passing me on the street with the windows open, blasting a song.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它更像是一辆车从我身边经过，车窗开着，大声播放着一首歌。

sentences.en: And you just hear a tiny snippet of the song and it takes you a while to recognize it.
sentences.zh: 你只听到了歌曲的一小段，需要花点时间才能认出来。

sentences.en: You know, like, you know, the song came out that one summer that you wore those denim cutoff shorts
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，这首歌是在那个夏天发行的，当时你穿着牛仔短裤，

sentences.en: and you were hanging out with your best friend and you definitely sang it at karaoke.
sentences.zh: 和最好的朋友在一起，你们肯定在卡拉OK唱过它。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's so familiar.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，它非常熟悉。

sentences.en: It's right on the tip of your tongue, but you just can't get it.
sentences.zh: 就在嘴边，但就是想不起来。

sentences.en: And then maybe 10 minutes later, you remember the name of the song.
sentences.zh: 然后可能过了10分钟，你记起了歌名。

sentences.en: When Chrissy and I kind of got to the end of our smell training session, she told me it's really about building confidence more than anything else.
sentences.zh: 当克丽丝和我在结束嗅觉训练时，她告诉我，这更多是为了建立信心，而不是其他任何东西。

sentences.en: It's about building up your confidence.
sentences.zh: 这是为了建立你的信心。

sentences.en: And before I spoke to Chrissy, I'd imagined smell training as being closer to like going to the gym or, you know, really cool, really active, really fun.
sentences.zh: 在和克丽丝交谈之前，我把嗅觉训练想象成去健身房，或者是非常酷、非常活跃、非常有趣的事情。

sentences.en: I'd sort of imagined, it's so embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 我曾想象过，这太尴尬了。

sentences.en: I'd sort of imagined like the Rocky theme song playing and I'm in like a cool tracksuit and I'm like jogging through Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 我曾想象《洛奇》的主题曲响起，我穿着酷炫的运动服，在洛杉矶慢跑。

sentences.en: And it's so boring and lonely to just sit and smell and think.
sentences.zh: 而只是坐着闻气味和思考，其实非常枯燥和孤独。

sentences.en: It can be kind of disheartening if you have a good day and then you have a bad day.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一天感觉很好，第二天又感觉很糟，这可能会让人感到沮丧。

sentences.en: It feels like you're going backwards.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像你在倒退。

sentences.en: I don't think that the word recovery is a good one to use because smell loss is an injury.
sentences.zh: 我不认为“康复”这个词用在这里很合适，因为嗅觉丧失是一种损伤。

sentences.en: So you recover from an illness, but an injury might leave you with some lasting scarring, you know.
sentences.zh: 你可以从疾病中康复，但损伤可能会留下一些持久的疤痕。

sentences.en: So if you were in a car accident and you were really badly banged up and had to have surgery or had scars somewhere, you wouldn't say, when am I going to recover from this?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你出了车祸，伤得很重，不得不做手术或者留下了疤痕，你不会问“我什么时候能从这件事中康复？”

sentences.en: You would say, when are my scars going to heal?
sentences.zh: 你会问“我的伤疤什么时候能愈合？”

sentences.en: You don't just go from hurt to healed overnight.
sentences.zh: 你不会一夜之间从受伤变得痊愈。

sentences.en: And that's what smell is like, you know.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉也是如此。

sentences.en: You don't just go back to normal.
sentences.zh: 你不会直接回到正常状态。

sentences.en: It's more like adjusting and learning how to live in a new space.
sentences.zh: 这更像是适应并学习如何在新的空间里生活。

sentences.en: It's really just the beginning.
sentences.zh: 这真的只是开始。

sentences.en: The smell training doesn't have a distinct timeline.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉训练没有明确的时间表。

sentences.en: I have been very tempted to stop because it's really, really tedious.
sentences.zh: 我曾多次想放弃，因为它真的非常非常乏味。

sentences.en: But over the weekend, I got a ladder out of the garage and propped it up against the lemon tree in my front yard.
sentences.zh: 但周末的时候，我从车库拿出一把梯子，靠在前院的柠檬树上。

sentences.en: And they have this amazing, like, floral, fruity perfume.
sentences.zh: 它们有一种迷人的、花香果味的香气。

sentences.en: And I noticed that the leaves, too, you know, I could smell the leaves.
sentences.zh: 我注意到叶子也是，我能闻到叶子的味道。

sentences.en: And there's something about it that feels new, too.
sentences.zh: 而且它有一种全新的感觉。

sentences.en: It feels so vivid.
sentences.zh: 感觉非常生动。

sentences.en: And I feel so grateful for it.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到非常感激。

sentences.en: In a way, I think I'm just paying much closer attention to it than I used to.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我想我只是比以前更加关注它了。

sentences.en: After two months, Tejal reports that her sense of smell has finally returned.
sentences.zh: 两个月后，Tejal报告说她的嗅觉终于恢复了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: We had a very tragic incident today here at the King Soopers.
sentences.zh: 今天在King Soopers发生了一起非常悲惨的事件。

sentences.en: There was loss of life.
sentences.zh: 有生命损失。

sentences.en: We have multiple people who were killed in this incident.
sentences.zh: 在这起事件中有多人遇难。

sentences.en: On Monday afternoon, a gunman opened fire at a grocery store in a residential neighborhood of Boulder, Colorado, killing 10 people, including a police officer.
sentences.zh: 周一下午，一名枪手在科罗拉多州博尔德市的一个居民区超市开枪，造成10人死亡，其中包括一名警察。

sentences.en: The suspected shooter is in custody, but the police have not described a motive.
sentences.zh: 嫌疑枪手已被拘留，但警方尚未说明动机。

sentences.en: It was the second mass shooting in less than a week, following the murder of eight people at spas in and around Atlanta, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 这是不到一周内的第二起大规模枪击事件，此前在佐治亚州亚特兰大及周边的水疗中心发生了导致8人死亡的谋杀案。

sentences.en: And the Times reports that on top of his nearly $2 trillion stimulus package, President Biden
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，除了近2万亿美元的刺激计划外，拜登总统

sentences.en: is preparing to recommend spending as much as $3 trillion on a sweeping set of new programs, beginning with a giant infrastructure plan.
sentences.zh: 正准备建议花费多达3万亿美元用于一系列广泛的新项目，首先是一个巨大的基础设施计划。

sentences.en: That plan calls for investing in roads, bridges, and rail lines, broadband internet for rural communities,
sentences.zh: 该计划呼吁投资道路、桥梁和铁路线，为农村社区提供宽带互联网，

sentences.en: charging stations for electric cars, and the construction of one million affordable housing units.
sentences.zh: 为电动汽车提供充电站，并建造一百万套经济适用房。

sentences.en: To pay for it, Biden is expected to propose raising taxes on corporations,
sentences.zh: 为了支付这些费用，预计拜登将提议提高企业税，

sentences.en: a tactic that is already meeting resistance from congressional Republicans, including Senator Mitch McConnell.
sentences.zh: 这一策略已经遭到国会共和党人的抵制，包括参议员米奇·麦康奈尔。

sentences.en: I think the Trojan horse will be called infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个特洛伊木马会被称为基础设施。

sentences.en: But inside the Trojan horse will be all the tax increases.
sentences.zh: 但特洛伊木马内部将是所有的增税措施。

sentences.en: Biden may seek to pass his infrastructure plan through a legislative process known as reconciliation
sentences.zh: 拜登可能会寻求通过一种称为“和解”的立法程序来通过他的基础设施计划，

sentences.en: that bypasses the need for Republican support in the Senate and requires just 51 votes rather than the usual 60.
sentences.zh: 该程序绕过了参议院对共和党支持的需求，只需51票而不是通常的60票。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I fully expect that's what they'll try to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我完全预料到他们会尝试这样做。

sentences.en: And that's because I don't think there's going to be any enthusiasm on our side for a tax increase.
sentences.zh: 那是因为我不认为我们这边会对增税有任何热情。

sentences.en: This episode was produced by Tina Antolini, edited by Wendy Doerr, engineered by Corey Schreppel, and contains original music by Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 本集由Tina Antolini制作，Wendy Doerr编辑，Corey Schreppel负责工程，并包含Dan Powell的原创音乐。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Hans Butow.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢Hans Butow。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是Michael Bavaro。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要完全遮光才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上找到《Wirecutter秀》。
